agents.author: Writes the files of a LADO kit (kit.yaml, roles, flows, skills, README) from an approved blueprint, and fixes them from the critic's report.
agents.critic: Evaluates a LADO kit, read-only, with `lado kits check`, the complexity budget and a 12-criterion rubric, and writes one report with quoted findings for the human.
agents.supervisor: Leads a kit-builder session — interviews the human about their process, writes the kit's blueprint, hands the writing to an author and the checking to a critic, and releases the kit.

kit-builder.description: Build and evaluate LADO kits. A supervisor interviews you about your process or starts from an archetype, writes a blueprint that says why each part of the kit exists, an author writes the kit and a critic checks it against a complexity budget and a rubric before release. The flow create takes a kit from interview to tag, improve takes an existing kit from the critic's report to a new tag, and evaluate reports on any kit. The blueprint, the plan and the reports are artifacts you read in LADO's UI.

agents.architect: Reviews a LADO design (not code) against ROADMAP, AGENTS.md and the current architecture, read-only, before it is implemented.
agents.checker: Runs LADO's full check, and the live tests a change needs, on a reviewed branch merged with main, before the human approves the merge; changes no code.
agents.developer: Implements one LADO task test-first on its own branch and reports with check output and a commit.
agents.reviewer: Reviews one LADO branch against its acceptance criteria, AGENTS.md and the long-term architecture, read-only, and gives a merge verdict.
agents.supervisor: Designs changes to LADO with the human for the long term, delegates them to an architect, developers, reviewers and a checker, and merges what passes review and the full check.

lado-dev.description: Develop LADO itself for the long term: a supervisor that designs with the human and delegates, an architect that reviews each design against the roadmap, developers that work test-first, reviewers that check each branch, and a checker that runs the full check before the human approves the merge; what anyone finds outside the task goes to BACKLOG.md. The flows feature and fix take each task from design to merge; each step's result (design, review, report, check results) is a run artifact the human reads in LADO's UI.

tracker-jira-server.description: The tracker skill for Jira Server / Data Center 8.4 or newer: find, read, create, move, comment on and link tasks through REST API v2, with a standard-library Python script. No agents: add it to a session next to a process kit.
